slice: exploring: five navigating observings, slime mould, spiny lobster, shearwater, godwit, bats

items.text: A slime mould, Physarum polycephalum, in a dish with oat flakes at the places of Greater Tokyo's cities and bright light where mountains, lakes and other obstacles are, a light the mould goes away from, spreads out and then thins its branches until only links between food sources go on: tubes with a fast flow widening, tubes with a slow flow thinning to nothing; the network it re-forms comes close to Tokyo's rail network, matching it in cost, in efficiency and in going on through a fault, with no plan. Each tube whose flow thins dissolves, and the network that is stands: from each is-not to is at a dish's scale, with no plan and no want.

Caribbean spiny lobsters, a person taking them away from where they live along a winding route with no useful chemical, visual or magnetic cue on the way, some boxes with swinging magnets, orient toward home on a tether in an arena, their eyes under a cover. In a further test, in a cage with the magnetic field of a place some 400 km north of home they walk south-southwest, and with a field of a place 400 km south they walk about north. Biology names it true navigation, the first in an invertebrate, the form of its map still-possibling: a self observing reads a lobster finding the field it stands in is-not home's field and aiming from that is-not to home, with no cue of its route.

Cory's shearwaters breeding in the Azores, a person setting them free on open ocean some 800 km from their colony: birds with a magnetic disturbance navigate about as well as birds with none, and birds with no sense of smell lose their orienting and homing dramatically, some wandering long, some coming home by chance or by sight, some not coming home. Over open sea, a sea's air is an orienting surface for a shearwater, a self orienting by the surface that is its own.

A bar-tailed godwit a tracker names E7 flies 11,680 km from Alaska to New Zealand in over eight days, no food, no water, no stopping; all the godwits a tracker follows set out with a favourable wind. A bird and a weather share one line: a departing co-sequencing with a wind, a bird co-linear with an air going toward its next.

items.section: 6.7 A school, a flock, a voyaging people, an orienting surface in no self alone
items.text: Bats leaving a roost the form of a corridor together, in a model by Mazar and Yovel that has each bat telling its own echoes from the others': with 100 bats about half of a bat's echoes from a wall a metre off go missing in the others' calls at each call, and still a bat goes on by gathering echoes across several calls, at 40 bats coming out about 20 times in 100 with one call's echoes and about 87 with ten; the model leaves out a bat hearing the others' echoes and following its neighbours, and its authors expect real bats to go on better. No one call is whole, and a sequence of calls goes nearer whole: a co-sequencing of many partial echoes in place of one whole signal.
